body:
## Pull request overview

Implements the `IMetadataService` contract in `@objectstack/metadata` by adding an in-memory registry layer on top of the existing loader pipeline, updating the `MetadataPlugin` to use `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` for type discovery/load ordering, and expanding tests to cover the contract surface.

**Changes:**
- `MetadataManager` now declares `implements IMetadataService` and adds CRUD, query, bulk, overlay, import/export, type registry, and dependency APIs.
- `MetadataPlugin` switches type discovery to `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` and registers loaded items into the manager registry during `start()`.
- Tests updated/added to validate the new contract behavior and the `list()` vs `listNames()` breaking change.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/metadata/vitest.config.ts | Adds vitest aliases for `@objectstack/spec/contracts` and `@objectstack/spec/kernel` imports used by the new implementation/tests. |
| packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts | Uses `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` for type discovery and initializes the manager with the default registry. |
| packages/metadata/src/metadata.test.ts | Updates existing tests to use `listNames()` and updates mocks to use `@objectstack/spec/kernel`. |
| packages/metadata/src/metadata-service.test.ts | Adds extensive tests for the `IMetadataService`-style behavior. |
| packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts | Core implementation of `IMetadataService` features (registry, query, overlay, import/export, dependencies, etc.). |
| packages/metadata/src/index.ts | Re-exports contract and kernel types to support downstream usage. |
</details>

`getEffective()` applies overlays via shallow object spread. The spec’s `MetadataOverlay.patch` is documented as JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396), which requires a recursive merge and supports deletions via `null`. With the current shallow merge, nested changes won’t apply correctly and `null` won’t remove keys. Consider using a JSON Merge Patch implementation (or a small recursive merge-patch utility) when applying `platform` and `user` patches.

`importMetadata()` destructures `validate` from options but never uses it. This makes the `validate` option misleading for callers and diverges from the contract docs (“Validate before import”). Either implement validation (e.g., call `this.validate(type, item)` when enabled) or remove the option from the signature if it’s intentionally unsupported.

`listNames()` calls `loader.list(type)` without any error handling. Other methods (e.g. `list()`/`loadMany()`) wrap loader failures to avoid taking down the whole operation. Consider adding try/catch around `loader.list` so a single loader failure doesn’t cause `listNames` to reject.

`MetadataManager` declares `implements IMetadataService`, but the class defines `watch(type, callback: WatchCallback): void` (legacy) which is incompatible with the contract’s optional `watch(type, callback: MetadataWatchCallback): MetadataWatchHandle`. With `implements`, TypeScript will try to match the `watch` member name and this should fail type-checking. Consider either (1) renaming the legacy `watch/unwatch` APIs, or (2) adding proper overloads so `watch` matches the contract signature and still supports the legacy callback type, and removing/aliasing `watchService` to `watch` for contract compliance.
